Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure occurs in the test `shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries` which expects an IOException to be thrown when reading a truncated tar archive. The failure report states that the TarArchiveInputStream silently finishes reading instead of throwing an IOException on unexpected EOF. 

From the `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` implementation, the method reads the next tar entry header using `getRecord()`. `getRecord()` calls `readRecord()`, which attempts to fully read a record-sized byte array from the underlying input stream.

If `readRecord()` does not read the full expected record size (indicating a truncated or premature EOF), it returns null. The returned null header buffer leads `getRecord()` to set `hasHitEOF` to true and subsequently return null without throwing an exception.

Back in `getNextTarEntry()`, it treats the null header buffer as EOF and returns null silently without an exception. This causes the stream to finish quietly instead of signaling the corruption via IOException.

The test expects an IOException as the truncated tar archive should not be silently accepted. However, the current implementation treats the truncated input as a normal EOF condition and returns null, resulting in no exception.

There is a catch block for `IllegalArgumentException` when parsing the tar header into `TarArchiveEntry`, but it is not triggered here because the truncated data leads to a null header rather than a malformed header.

Thus, the core issue lies in the treatment of unexpected EOF during header reading: silent EOF detection combined with a null return from `getNextTarEntry()` rather than throwing an IOException when incomplete header data is encountered.

Recent bug reports related to tar entry parsing issues (e.g., invalid byte in user-id) show exceptions thrown on parsing errors but do not address silent EOF cases. This confirms the current bug stems from unhandled premature EOF condition in reading headers.

Recommended fix is to detect incomplete header record during `readRecord()`, and propagate this as an IOException or a dedicated exception from `getNextTarEntry()` rather than returning null for malformed/truncated entries. 

This way, clients like the failing test will observe exceptions and handle corrupted truncated tar archives as expected.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
